/home/hatch/workspace/outreach/pipeline.md:54:- Snow removal (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 5 verified candidates. Mid-September lands squarely in the snow contract-signing window (September through November), the segment's highest-intent inbound period. Own-site evidence documents storm cleanups starting 2-3am with 14-16 hour storm days; storm-morning call chaos, route-capacity pressure, early-hour dispatch, and seasonal contract renewals are the missed-call pain PING targets. Commercial operators with multi-crew routes (D&D Asphalt, Summit Sweeping, Grasshoppers) are the strongest fits. Thinner than expected under the own-site rule; mostly landscaping/asphalt hybrids, phone-primary. If the pool thins, revisit phone-primary near-misses (Peaceful Valley, J&J Snow Removal) or Facebook engagement.
/home/hatch/workspace/outreach/pipeline.md:64:- Asphalt / paving (Western Colorado, research batch round 24, 2026-09-11): new segment, 8 qualified. September is the tail of Colorado's paving season (May through October); sealcoat needs sustained pavement temps above 50F, so HOA and commercial lot rush before winter is the urgent demand trigger. Crews are on pavers, rollers, and sealcoat rigs all day and cannot answer; estimate follow-up is the pitch. Grand Junction is crowded; Glenwood/Rifle/Carbondale and Durango/Cortez/Pagosa coverage is thinner; Cortez, Pagosa Springs, Craig, and Meeker produced no own-site-verified shops. Software UNKNOWN across all 17 researched; no booking widgets or CRM badges anywhere. Skip patterns: franchise systems (Jet-Black), white-label template farms (Animas Asphalt's "CPS" copy), out-of-state bases. Several strong local shops have weak or no websites (Kauffman, High Country, JB's, CM Asphalt), which is both a pipeline gap and an inbound angle: thin web presence correlates with phone-only workflows and high missed-call pain.
